w: Today, a continuous chanting of the Swaminarayan Mahamantra was organised in the mandir from 6.00 a.m. From the city’s 48 areas, devotees from 39 areas chanted the Swaminarayan mantra while they walked together to the mandir.

After puja, while Swamishri was returning to his residence by car, Swamishri saw the devotees chanting the dhun. Swamishri had his car stopped and he stepped out and started clapping and chanting the dhun. The devotees were overwhelmed with joy. Swamishri asked for the microphone and began chanting the dhun for the next five minutes.
( See Special Report )

st.t: Shri Hari Jayanti Festival, Bhavnagar, 12 April 2000
w: The 220th birthday anniversary of Lord Swaminarayan was celebrated with devotion and jubilation in the presence of HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj in Bhavnagar. From early morning thousands of devotees arrived from neighboring towns and villages to celebrate Shri Hari Jayanti. Members from twelve villages pilgrimaged on foot (padyatra) to Bhavnagar. A fifty-five-year old devotee prostrated his way from Mahuva to Bhavnagar - 11,000 prostrations. The morning puja of Swamishri was charged with devotional bhajans describing the divine form and acts of Lord Swaminarayan. The main evening assembly was held at 'Akshar Vadi'. The festival program comprised of speeches, bhajans and a powerpoint presentation on the life and work of Lord Swaminarayan interspersed with live drama presentations on Abhaysinh's steadfastness, transformation of Joban Pagi, honesty of Govind Bhagat and the faith of Devji Bhagat. A colorful dance was performed by children and teenage members celebrating the birth of Lord Swaminarayan on the lyric, "Chaitra sud navmi avi…" Swamishri then blessed the 15,000 devotees and wellwishers, saying, "Today, for us and the entire people of India, it is the greatest day because God came in human form on earth to redeem countless people and to show us the right path. Through our willful or imaginative means we cannot achieve peace and happiness in life. The highest path to attain inner peace is one given to us by God and His holy sadhus and sages. Lord Swaminarayan gave the Shikshapatri for the good of all souls. One cannot achieve happiness or moksha without the knowledge of atma and Paramatma. Only when one attains the state of akshar-roop and offers devotion to Purushottam, does one experience absolute peace. And then despite living in this world, one remains detached from all mundane desires…" The assembly climaxed with the arti performed by Swamishri and the devotees. Victory cries of "Sahajanand Swami Maharaj ni jay…", "Dharma gher anand bhayo…" Swamishri gently rocked the murti of Lord Harikrishna Maharaj in a decorated traditional cot. The assembly dispersed in a joyous and spiritual mood.

At 6.30 pm, Swamishri departed from Dubai International Airport and landed in Bahrain after a one hour flight. Swamishri was welcomed by Dr. Prafulbhai Vaidya, Jasbirsingh, Vinay Diwan and other devotees.

The Best of Devotees A few verses from the biography of Bhagwan Swaminarayan - 'Haricharitramrut Sagar' by Adharanand Swami - were read before Swamishri: "There is no greater sinner among devotees than one who speaks ill of another devotee. He is the best of devotees who sees his own faults." On hearing this verse a devotee remarked, "Bapa, this is very difficult to avoid. We see faults in others and not in our ownselves." Swamishri replied, "Because we fail to see our faults it has been so instructed. When you find fault in someone then you should introspect whether you've got it yourself. Someone may have lust whereas you may have greed. Someone may have jealousy whereas you may have ego. Our faults are written on our back whereas we see others' on their chest ..." "But Swamishri, it is only through divine grace that one can overcome this," a devotee added. "Yes. Only through grace can one realize this. That is why it has been said, 'Hari krupa jab hovat he, tab sujat apna dosh' (Only through God's grace can one see one's own faults). When we do 'seva' to please the Guru only, only then does one's base nature dissolves ..."
Riches bring fame but it increases the inclinations of faultfinding, enmity and ego.
By slowly bringing garbage in a clean home, the entire house will become full. Similarly, by looking at faults in others one will become full of faults.

To cater to students of higher secondary level from grade 8 to 12, the BAPS has planned to build an educational complex on the outskirts of Nagpur city. Swamishri performed the bhumi-pujan rituals by sprinkling kum kum, rice grains and flowers amidst Vedic chantings. Thereafter Swamishri sanctified the land by sprinkling flowers.
After his morning puja Swamishri performed the pujan rituals of murtis for the Kutir Mandir in Vaghamba (S. Gujarat).
A youth came for darshan. He said, "My addictions do not go."
Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "If you have to go to London or America, can you leave your house here or not?"
"Yes."
"Even though the house is your own, you leave it?"
"Yes."
Swamishri said, "We leave even what is our own, so this has come from outside. How long should it take to leave it? Leave it."

A youth named Kaushikbhai Modi said to Pramukh Swami Maharaj, "Until today I had only indulged in addictions, but when I came into contact with you, every addiction left me. Even my friends are amazed. In fact my duty is in a bar, so I have to serve people liquor, but even amid that, by your grace, I do not feel like drinking. After the Chandkheda centenary festival, everything changed. After that many temptations came, but I have not drunk at all."

Tonight Pramukh Swami Maharaj was coming back to his residence after casting his glance on the water show. It was about 8:40. Darkness had fallen. Swamishri was coming towards his residence in his wheelchair. In the Akshardham premises, lights were on only where needed. Although the doors of Akshardham had been closed, as he passed, Swamishri bowed and had darshan.
As the wheelchair moved along, Swamishri asked Dharmakunvar Swami, who had come from Bhadra and was among the sadhus walking quickly behind, "How are the preparations for the installation going?"
Dharmakunvar Swami spoke about everything from accommodation to the building of the mandir and the renovation of the old mandir. In five minutes Swamishri got a full picture of the preparations.
Swamishri's wheelchair was moving along, with light falling ahead from a mobile tubelight and the beam of a torch. Even at such a time, Swamishri made use of the time.
On one occasion all the sadhus were sitting before Pramukh Swami Maharaj and talks were going on. During the conversation, Yagnesh Swami said, "What are your wishes?"
Swamishri said, "The wishes Yogiji Maharaj made cannot all be fulfilled, so why should we make separate ones? We are trying to fulfil his wishes."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Never mind other wishes, but come, make one wish."

Swamishri said, "There is none. Yogiji Maharaj made wishes and they have been fulfilled. How many more should we make? Yogiji Maharaj used to speak of colouring the universe, of making satsang grow, of the number of sadhus growing. We are moving within those very wishes of his."
Narayancharan Swami said, "Your wishes are Yogiji Maharaj's wishes, aren't they! So whatever you make would be called Yogiji Maharaj's, wouldn't it!"
Laughing, Swamishri said, "It is you who think they are separate. We do not think so at all."
Vishwavihari Swami said, "Come, make one wish, that you will stay on this earth for another 100 years and fulfil Yogiji Maharaj's wishes."
Dharmavatsal Swami said, "Why a hundred? A hundred and twenty five."
Laughing, Swamishri said, "Why even a hundred and twenty five? Say more!"
Yagnesh Swami said, "We would certainly say more, but the wish is that you travel in this very same body."
Swamishri said, "Has it (the body) ever stayed for anyone? One should believe only that one is the atma."
Narayancharan Swami said, "But please keep it."

Swamishri said, "He (Yogiji Maharaj) will keep it. We depend on God. The work is done through him. Nothing is done by us. If one says, 'I do it, I do it,' one is finished. If ego comes, 'I did this, I did that,' it is all over. But if one behaves as the atma, whether there is honour, insult or contempt, nothing will matter."
On one occasion, talk turned to Bhagatji Maharaj.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "Just like Nachiketa, Bhagatji Maharaj too asked Gunatitanand Swami only for knowledge of the atma. Even while enduring hardships, he asked for knowledge of the atma. When Gunatitanand Swami said to Bhagatji Maharaj, 'Ask for a boon,' and also offered temptations, Bhagatji Maharaj said only this: 'If you are pleased, give me the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam.' His (Nachiketa's) story was very long ago. That is a story of the Vedic age, but he (Bhagatji Maharaj) lived only recently. Shastriji Maharaj also served Bhagatji Maharaj. We are talking about the manifest form, but 'I know how to swim and how to dive, but presence of mind is forgotten.'"
Having said this, Swamishri said, "Well, Pandit! Is that right?"
Shrutiprakash Swami said, "We forget. Because of our natures and faults we forget everything, and so the joy of the atma and Paramatma lessens."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "We fail to forget honour and insult and enjoy the bliss of God."
Swamishri said, "Where is there any question of honour and insult? How can all this get in the way of one who has become brahmarup?"

Having said this, Swamishri began to sing, "Oneness in honour and insult, equanimity in happiness and misery; yes, such is the good sadhu..." Yogiji Maharaj used to sing this kirtan often. "'This happened to me and that happened to me, I got this and I did not get that,' all that would not happen at all. There would be only oneness in honour and insult. If there is honour, it is God's grace, and if there is insult, it is God's wish. Whether misery comes or happiness comes, nothing happens except by his wish. If one thinks like this, there is no unhappiness at all, no regret at all."

ds.t: We only fulfil Yogiji Maharaj's resolves
w: Once the sadhus were all sitting before Swamishri and talking. During the conversation Yagnesh Swami said, "What are your resolves?"
Swamishri said, "All the resolves Yogiji Maharaj made cannot even be completed, so why should we make separate ones? We are only trying to fulfil his resolves."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Never mind other resolves, but come, make one resolve."

Swamishri said, "There is none. We fulfil the resolves Yogiji Maharaj made; how many more should we make? Yogiji Maharaj spoke of colouring the universe, of growing satsang, of more sadhus. We go on within those resolves of his."
Narayancharan Swami said, "Your resolves are Yogiji Maharaj's resolves! So whatever you make would be called Yogiji Maharaj's!"
Laughing, Swamishri said, "You are the ones who think they are separate. Where do we think so?"
Vishwavihari Swami said, "Come, make one resolve: that you will stay on this earth another 100 years to fulfil Yogiji Maharaj's resolves."
Dharmavatsal Swami said, "Why a hundred? A hundred and twenty five."
Laughing, Swamishri said, "Why even a hundred and twenty five? Say more!"
Yagnesh Swami said, "We will say more, but our resolve is that you travel in this very same body."
Swamishri said, "Has that (body) ever stayed for anyone? Believe only that we are the soul."
Narayancharan Swami said, "But please keep it."

Swamishri said, "He (Yogiji Maharaj) will keep it. We depend on God. The work gets done through Him. Nothing happens by us. If one keeps saying 'I do, I do', one is finished. If pride comes, 'I did this, I did that', it is over. But if one lives as the soul, then honour, insult or scorn, nothing troubles."
Once the talk turned to Bhagatji Maharaj.

Swamishri said, "Just like Nachiketa, Bhagatji Maharaj asked Gunatitanand Swami only for knowledge of the soul. Even bearing suffering, he asked for knowledge of the soul. When Gunatitanand Swami told Bhagatji Maharaj, 'Ask for a boon,' and even offered temptations, Bhagatji Maharaj said only, 'If you are pleased, give me the knowledge of Akshar Purushottam.' That (Nachiketa's) story is from long ago, from the Vedic age, but these lived only recently. Shastriji Maharaj too served Bhagatji Maharaj. We speak only of the manifest, but 'I know how to swim and how to dive, but I forget my presence of mind.'"
Saying this, Swamishri said, "Isn't that right, Pandit?"
Shrutiprakash Swami said, "We forget. Because of our natures and faults we forget everything, so the joy of the soul and God lessens."
Brahmavihari Swami said, "Caught up in honour and insult, we miss out on the joy of God."
Swamishri said, "Where is there any question of honour and insult? For one who has become brahmarup, how can all this get in the way?"

Saying this, Swamishri began to sing: "'Oneness in honour and insult, evenness in happiness and sorrow; yes sir, good sadhu...' Yogiji Maharaj used to sing this kirtan a lot. 'This happened to me, that happened to me, I got this, I did not get that', none of that happens at all. There is only oneness in honour and insult. If honour comes, it is God's grace, and if insult comes, it is God's wish. Whether sorrow comes or happiness, nothing happens except by His wish. With such thinking, sorrow never comes and there is no regret."

Mahant Swami Maharaj was to leave here today. The African manager of the hotel where Swamishri was staying came for Swamishri's darshan. He said, "I want a murti of this very guru who has come." And he also put on a kanthi (sacred necklace).
Just as everyone naturally experiences the fragrance of a flower, so the divinity of the great sadhu naturally touches everyone; this was experienced here.

When Mahant Swami Maharaj sat for his meal, talk turned to the terrible accident Harinarayandas Swami had had a few days earlier, and how, by Swamishri's power, his health was improving in an amazing way. He had bleeding in the very place where one breathes, in the lungs. The sadhus said to Swamishri, "You said, 'It will seal,' and within a short time it sealed...!"
This was a significant and big thing, because there is no medicine at all to stop that bleeding.
And the sadhus said, "Today is only the 12th day, and yet he has recovered so well! This is nothing but a miracle."
Feeding him, Gunvatsaldas Swami said, "You protected him."
Swamishri said, "Bhagwan protected him."
Swamishri immediately poured all the credit on the head of his Ishtadev.
In the evening assembly, in keeping with today's Kishore Day, the sorry plight of a young man who goes mad in love was presented very beautifully through a live dialogue.
On this occasion, giving inspiring blessings, Mahant Swami Maharaj spoke loving words:

"The point here is that if there is extremely firm faith in the great sadhu, all the work gets done. People have faith in a friend worth two paise and dance as he makes them dance, but they do not have faith in the great sadhu. Yogi Bapa and Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, 'Sense pleasures are perishable.' If one believes this, one can stay away from them. There are thousands of friends; there is only one great sadhu. (There was much applause.) If one girlfriend leaves, you get another, a third... 'Do din ki chandni phir andheri raat' (two days of moonlight, then a dark night). After five years of marriage, faces become like this (he twisted his face to show)! If faith comes, everything else comes. If you have faith in the vaidya, in the doctor, then the pill works. One has faith even in the barber, doesn't one, that he will not run the razor across one's throat! One gives him one's head. But faith in the great sadhu does not come. This is not blind faith. Look at the great sadhu's work, look at his life. If you have truly associated with him, you will understand this and then faith will come. Faults of nature and so on will go, but if there is faith, the work will be done.

In short, keep firm faith in the great sadhu and do just as he says. He has no selfish motive. He has two pieces of cloth and wants nothing else. He eats two mouthfuls and works 18 hours a day; there is no reason for it. If we look at his life, we realise that he is selfless. Whether we love him or not, he loves us! Stick to the great sadhu. The great sadhu is a good place to put your faith. The niyams that seem hard to us he keeps naturally. Look at his devotion, look at his seva. Yogi Bapa would grab the seva of scrubbing pots. We were all just like you. But Yogi Bapa transformed us like this (he made a gesture of transformation). Faith came. And his was a life that inspired faith; why would faith not come? There is no need to attach yourself anywhere else apart from this. Those who became attached to Yogi Bapa and Pramukh Swami Maharaj have joy upon joy."

On the occasion of Kishore Day, a card had been prepared so that all the teenage boys and girls would get a special memory. In it, a question had been asked on their behalf: "Mahant Swami Maharaj, what is your wish that we should never break, so that we may have firm love for you?"
Swamishri wrote wonderful answers, which will be an inspiration for everyone:
1. Firmness in keeping niyams:
a. In this, do not eat outside food.
b. Give up watching garba.
c. Keep the boundaries between men and women.
d. Keep vows and fasts according to your faith.
2. And there must be firm conviction.
If you behave like this, Maharaj, Swami and Swami Bapa will be very pleased. It will be said that you have lived according to their wish.
